judged_text: updateEvent's calendar selection is a tautology: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it searches for a calendar whose externalId equals null/undefined and always returns undefined. For any booking reference without externalCalendarId (legacy references), selectedCalendar becomes undefined where the old code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`; google.calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined, so reschedules fail with a Google API 'required parameter calendarId' error instead of updating the destination calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. The `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId` equals `undefined/null`, which will normally return `undefined`. Unlike `createEvent` (which falls back to `"primary"`), the `updateEvent` path shown does not add a fallback and will pass an undefined `calendarId` into `calendar.events.update`, matching the described Google API failure for legacy references without `externalCalendarId`.
